dedupe_keys.name: epa landfill gas emissions model landgem version 3 1

description: LandGEM is the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's model for estimating air emissions from municipal solid waste landfills. From the landfill's design capacity, the waste in place or the annual acceptance rate, the methane generation rate and potential, concentrations of nonmethane organic compounds, the years of operation and whether hazardous waste was co-disposed, it estimates emissions of total landfill gas, methane, carbon dioxide, nonmethane organic compounds and individual pollutants over time, treating landfill gas as roughly half methane and half carbon dioxide. Owners and operators use it to check whether a landfill falls under federal New Source Performance Standards, Emission Guidelines or hazardous air pollutant standards. The provider is the EPA Office of Research and Development; the current release is the Version 3.1 user manual and tool (Krause and Thorneloe, EPA/600/B-24/160, 2024). Coverage is any municipal solid waste landfill, with site-specific data or default parameters. The tool is a free macro-enabled Excel workbook using Visual Basic for Applications, tested on Office 2007 and later, and downloaded through the EPA Science Inventory. Caveats: runs on default parameters give only rough estimates where site data are missing, the model estimates generation and emissions, not gas collection or fire behaviour, and it is a spreadsheet, not open source code. Simulation uses: methane generation inputs for landfill energy recovery and fire risk, and emissions scenarios under changed waste flows after disasters. Related records: the EDF landfill methane map (data-edf-landfill-methane-map) shows observed emissions.
